q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a spanner or other hand tool?
title: Hand tool carbon footprint per piece
short: Take the steel bar per tool, including flash and scale lost in forging, and multiply by the steel supplier's per-kg figure. Add forging furnace fuel, heat treatment, machining and plating electricity, then divide by tools passed.
audience: Hand tool makers in Jalandhar and Ludhiana

ul: Alloy steel bar by weight per tool, including flash.
Forging furnace fuel or induction heater electricity.
Grinding, polishing and chrome or nickel plating.

p: Report per tool with its weight. Group tools by weight band rather than one average across a whole catalogue.

example.title: Worked example: spanner and hand tool unit per piece (one month)
lines: Plant total: 44,250 / 120,000 = 0.369 kg CO2 per piece
Add steel and plating for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
